title: Compress the process
summary: Reduce support step by step across 45-minute, 35-minute and 30-minute composition rehearsals while protecting task fit, a compact plan, complete development and a meaning-first final check.

sections.title: Compress time, not the writing process
content: The current reported profile gives composition a separate 30-minute period, but the prompt families and approximate length guidance remain provisional. Timed practice should therefore build a transferable process rather than train one memorised essay or invent a rigid words-per-minute rule.

Keep four non-negotiable jobs at every stage: answer the actual task, make a compact route, develop the response to a complete ending and reserve a meaning-first check. Compression removes delay and unnecessary support; it does not remove the decisions that keep the writing relevant and coherent.

sections.title: Use 45 minutes to expose the real bottleneck
content: Begin with a fresh 45-minute supported rehearsal. A visible prompt-decoding checklist, planning frame and time signals may remind the learner which process step comes next, but they must not supply ideas, sentences or corrections. Record when planning ends, drafting ends and checking begins, plus every support actually used.

Treat this run as a diagnosis rather than an easy score. A response that finishes early but drifts from the prompt is not ready to compress. A complete response that needs twelve minutes to choose its focus has revealed a planning bottleneck that can be practised directly before the next stage.

sections.title: Remove one support for the 35-minute rehearsal
content: Use a fresh comparable prompt at 35 minutes. Replace the full planning frame with a compact task–focus–paragraph-route note, keep neutral time signals and remove mid-draft prompting. Change one bottleneck at a time so the result can show whether the shorter process transferred rather than whether the learner remembered the earlier response.

Suppose the 45-minute record shows a complete answer with six minutes of checking, while the 35-minute record is complete with four minutes of checking but has an overlong opening and a thin second reason. The next action is not to delete planning or checking. It is to cap the opening, preserve the compact route and practise developing the second reason on another fresh prompt.

sections.title: Protect a valid 30-minute independent run
content: Attempt 30 minutes only after the 35-minute record is complete enough to justify less support. Use a fresh prompt, one separately controlled clock and no hints, model answers, external editing or feedback before submission. Do not borrow unused time from another section. Record any genuine interruption and interpret the run cautiously if its conditions change.

Use time signals as decision points, not as a rigid allocation that must fit every prompt. A bounded opening protects prompt decoding and a compact plan; most time belongs to drafting; a final signal stops expansion while a short checking buffer remains. If the route needs simplifying, reduce repetition or optional detail before sacrificing the ending or the check.

sections.title: Recover without abandoning the whole response
content: When time is running short, protect coverage in order. Confirm the response still answers the prompt, finish the central route with a bounded conclusion, repair the largest missing explanation, then check sentence boundaries and high-risk conventions. Do not open a new reason merely to make the response longer.

A compact plan should be quick to scan and cheap to change. Use keywords and arrows rather than drafted sentences. If one paragraph stalls, mark the intended claim and consequence, continue to the next planned job and return only if the checking buffer permits.

sections.title: Interpret pacing evidence honestly
content: Classify the main loss as planning overflow, drafting stall, incomplete development, missing ending, checking loss or contaminated conditions. Choose one repair for the next fresh prompt. Repeating an exposed prompt may build fluency, but its faster time cannot by itself demonstrate transfer to unseen writing.

One fast run is not an official readiness score or an admission prediction. If the 30-minute response is incomplete or depends on help, return to the 35-minute stage, target the recorded bottleneck and try another fresh comparable prompt. Progress means preserving a complete independent process under less time, not merely producing more words.

sections.title: Choose a safe compression route
content: Use a fictional three-run practice record. Make six decisions about staged support, relevant evidence, targeted compression, independent conditions, time recovery and honest interpretation before viewing feedback.
